purpose: Ground the post-P0 T5 development plan in observed work and expectations of solo business owners, freelancers, creators, and small-business generalists rather than a feature inventory.

sources.sample: more than 5,000 SMEs in seven countries including Korea
more than 2,200 US businesses with up to 100 employees
16,000 creators in eight countries including South Korea

observations.requiredBoundary: AI accelerates the workflow while creative control remains human

sources.sample: 261 freelancers and 6,525 observations on one Korean platform

observations.demandShift: Individuals internalize simple creation; business demand shifts toward refining and verifying AI-generated drafts.
observations.researchLimit: One platform and a small role-specific sample; do not generalize to every freelance occupation.

observations.interpretation: AI can diffuse stronger workers' practices but does not remove the need for human responsibility or domain judgement.

observations.principle: AI improves work inside its uneven capability frontier and can reduce performance outside it; similar-looking tasks require different verification.
Showing meaningful work being performed can increase perceived effort, value and trust even when the objective result is unchanged.
observations.boundary: Transparency cannot rescue a poor process and should not expose irrelevant internal machinery.

observations.principle: Waiting-duration information may not shorten perceived duration, but can preserve a sense of control and improve acceptance and service-quality evaluation.

methodCaveats: Adoption rates are not comparable across surveys because populations, industries, countries, and the definition of AI use differ.
Vendor-commissioned surveys can overrepresent customers already disposed to use the vendor's products.
Online community reports are qualitative workflow signals, not prevalence estimates.
External research cannot replace direct observation of consenting T5 target users and their actual work artifacts.
derivedHumanWorkDomains: win work: market research, positioning, website, content, proposal, estimate
receive and manage customers: inquiry, booking, preparation, follow-up, CRM facts
deliver expert work: research and drafts around the user's professional judgement
operate the business: email, calendar, files, tasks, contracts, billing, settlement
improve the business: review, inquiry, content, sales and cost evidence into changes
monitor and repeat: daily exceptions, weekly performance, monthly reconciliation
derivedExperienceExpectations: smooth continuity across sessions, devices, channels, files and apps
compatibility with the user's existing environment rather than migration into T5-specific formats
capabilities that expand and retire without making the user administer an agent framework
predictable current state, next observation and stop path without fabricated completion estimates
operational transparency based on actual runtime events rather than hidden chain-of-thought or decorative status text
trust through source, execution, effect, uncertainty, recovery and result evidence
a revisable understanding of the user without permanent persona classification
humanOwnedBoundary: final price, contract, legal, tax, medical and payment decisions
t5DelegatedBoundary: collect, locate, read and connect current sources
prepare native result artifacts and previews
monitor repeated work and surface exceptions

realityCorpusTarget.privacy: Keep no production personal data in the repository; preserve workflow structure with synthetic identities and values.
